newsitem.title: INDIA: Police disperse India SWC shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Police disperse India SWC shareholders.

text.p: Police in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta used batons on Friday, to disperse shareholders of liquor firm Shaw Wallace and Company Ltd, (SWC) who tried to enter an overcrowded hall to attend the company's annual meeting.
"We had to chase out the shareholders as there was no place inside the hall," a police official told Reuters.

The shareholders became agitated when they were refused entry inside the hall, witnesses said. They alleged that shareholders who were in the company's labour union had forcibly captured most of the seats.
The meeting failed to adopt any of the eight resolutions listed for approval as some of the shareholders demanded a vote before their adoption.
The resolutions included one approving the accounts for 1995/96 (April-March) and another seeking the re-appointment of the company's chairman, M.R. Chhabria, as a director.
The firm's managing director, R.K. Jain, said voting on all the resolutions will he held on Sunday.
Jain, who presided over the meeting in absence of Chhabria, said the company had prepared a blueprint for restructuring.
He said the company would continue to lay stress on its liquor division and had decided to keep in abeyance a fund-raising programme.
"We have decided to stick to our core areas of liquor and beer and achieve such economies of scale that would give us an edge over competitors in the domestic and overseas market," Jain said.
Though its chief interest lies in liquor, Shaw Wallace has divisions making consumer products like soaps and cosmetics.
